sources.citation: Zobel, Erik. 2018. The South Babar languages of southwest Maluku. Web page, ezlinguistics.blogspot.com (accessed this compilation).
sources.note: Historical phonology based on Taber's lists; only stress remark is reconstructive: 'In stressed (= penultimate) position, all four vowels remain distinct' (Proto Southwest Maluku > Proto South Babar vowel history); unstressed final-syllable vowels 'underwent drastic reduction.. leaving a zero reflex in many South Babar lects'. Nothing synchronic about East Masela stress.

sources.note: For WEST DAMAR: MS p. 9 'Chlenova (2008) informs that most West-Damar items in the wordlist are bisyllabic or trisyllabic. sources.citation: Steinhauer, Hein. 2009. The sounds of Southeast Babar. In K. A. Adelaar & A. Pawley (eds.), Austronesian historical linguistics and culture history: a festschrift for Robert Blust (Pacific Linguistics 601), 91-105. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: About the SISTER language Southeast Babar (sout2883), not East Masela: p.96 'Stress does not seem to be phonemic at the word level. Often the same word occurs with different stress in comparable environments. Below I refrain with some exceptions from indicating stress.' East Masela appears only in the discussion of Taber's classification (pp. 92-93 fn.).

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press (sec. 4.6.5 Babar, pp. 224-236).
sources.note: Nothing on East Marsela stress. p.224: 'The 193-item word lists in Taber (1993) are the only source of data for five of these languages: Dai [dij], North Babar [bcd], East Marsela [vme], Imroing [imr], and Tela-Masbuar [tvm].' fn.26: Edwards' 2025 field data on all South Babar languages archived as Edwards (2023a), not integrated. East Marsela forms are cited only in re-phonemicised, stress-less form in the sound-correspondence tables.

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2023a- (fieldwork 2025, items added Oct 2025 and Jul 2026). Emplawas and languages of the Babar islands. Endangered Languages Archive deposit 0741, hdl:2196/28f40694-81ac-4d06-b515-617dd6469394 - East Marsela sessions VME001-VME012 plus 2026 narrative/procedural bundles (e.g. VME011 'Child who became a stone', 'History of Mepal', 'Farming 11', 'Fish traps 3', 'Making palmwine 1', with ELAN.eaf transcriptions).
sources.note: Re-checked because new sessions were added since the reading: item descriptions (VME011 read in full) give story summaries, participants and file lists only; the earlier-read wordlist items describe vowel inventories (six or seven vowels) and transcription conventions; no statement on stress, accent or tone anywhere; no sketch/phonology document deposited. Primary data only (audio, video.eaf).

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2023a (ongoing, 2025 fieldwork). Emplawas and languages of the Babar islands. Endangered Languages Archive, hdl:2196/28f40694-81ac-4d06-b515-617dd6469394 — 12 'Marsela, East' items.
sources.note: Only modern first-hand documentation of East Marsela (wordlist elicitation with audio by a phonologist); any accompanying transcription notes or a future Babar 'language snapshot'/sketch by Edwards would supersede everything else.

sources.citation: van Engelenhoven, Aone. 1997. [Review of] Mark Taber, Leslie A. Forster, Charles E. Grimes, et al., eds. 1996. Atlas Bahasa Tanah Maluku. Cakalele 8: 91-108 (reviews section; this review pp. 91-94). Honolulu: Center for Southeast Asian Studies. ScholarSpace hdl 10125/4231.
sources.note: No phonology. Describes the Atlas as shaded maps based on SIL lexicostatistics, an appendix on local Malay, a bibliography, and 'additional informal notes on how the language speakers live and how they can be reached' - i.e. no structural notes per language, consistent with the p. xi statement that stress is not represented.

sources.citation: Taber, Mark. 1993. Toward a better understanding of the indigenous languages of Southwestern Maluku. Oceanic Linguistics 32(2): 389-441 — East Masela 193-item list as re-keyed in LexiRumah 3.0.0 (Kaiping, Edwards & Klamer 2019, lect east2462) and ABVD language 312.
sources.note: Primary data only: phonetic forms carry Taber's stress mark. Tabulated (script) over 189 forms: 76 monosyllables, 91 stress on first syllable of a disyllable/penult (ˈrowek 'sky', ˈtahal 'knife', mo-ˈvorei 'know'), 13 final (oˈlei 'tree', oiˈmɛl 'man', mə-ˈloip 'run', mostly prefix+monosyllabic root), 8 antepenult (ˈirəmok 'face'), 1 unmarked. No prose statement (the article text itself, JSTOR, was not accessible).
